meta.purpose: Machine-readable inventory of everything that must move when the product changes hands, excluding the source history itself.
notes: status is 'pre-transfer' until every obligation has a named_person and every acceptance is signed; scripts/check_handover.py --strict enforces exactly that.
Prices live in docs/HANDOVER.md, not here: they change, and this file is a custody record.

keys.name: JWT signing secret
keys.purpose: Signs admin session tokens for the dashboard API.
keys.loss_impact: All admins are logged out once. No data is lost, no device is affected.
keys.transfer_action: Generate fresh with `openssl rand -hex 32` in the receiving environment. Never transfer the value.

keys.name: Legacy shared agent key
keys.purpose: Transitional fallback auth for devices that have no per-device API key hash yet.
keys.loss_impact: Any device still on the legacy path stops authenticating until it is re-enrolled; devices with per-device keys are unaffected.
keys.transfer_action: Count legacy devices first (`api_key_hash IS NULL`). If zero, generate fresh and drop the variable entirely.

keys.name: Per-device API key pepper
keys.purpose: Peppers the hash of every per-device agent API key.
keys.loss_impact: Every stored api_key_hash becomes unverifiable: the entire fleet fails authentication and must be re-enrolled in person.
keys.transfer_action: Travels with the database. If the DB does not transfer, generate fresh and re-enrol.

keys.name: Field encryption key (at rest)
keys.purpose: Encrypts sensitive columns at rest (FA2).
keys.loss_impact: Encrypted columns are unreadable permanently. There is no recovery path — not even a DB restore helps.
keys.transfer_action: Travels with the database, in a sealed escrow, never in a chat or a commit.

keys.name: Location field key
keys.purpose: Separate at-rest key for location reports (FA5) — deliberately a different blast radius from K-FIELD-ENC.
keys.loss_impact: All historical location data is unreadable. Because this is personal data under GDPR, losing the key is a deletion event that also has to be recordable.
keys.transfer_action: Travels with the database. Do not merge it into K-FIELD-ENC to simplify the handover.

keys.name: Backup encryption key
keys.purpose: AES-256-CBC key for every backup the server writes (service is on by default).
keys.loss_impact: Every existing backup becomes an unreadable blob. The DR runbook stops being executable.
keys.transfer_action: Travels with the backup set OR is shared out-of-band before the first restore drill.

keys.name: Agent update signing key (Ed25519) + pinned public key
keys.purpose: Signs `/api/agent/update` metadata (`v1:{version}:{sha256}`). Agents pin the public key, so a SHA-256 alone is not self-certifying.
keys.loss_impact: Every deployed agent already trusts this exact key. Lose the private key and no agent can be updated again; rotate it and every agent must be re-enrolled to accept the new pin.
keys.transfer_action: The only secret that must transfer even when the database does not. Escrow both halves; record the key id in the acceptance table.

keys.name: Recovery escrow keypair
keys.purpose: Out-of-band unlock path for a locked device. Deliberately a different key domain from K-UPDATE-SIGN.
keys.loss_impact: A locked device in the field has no software unlock path left; recovery becomes a physical/BIOS exercise.
keys.transfer_action: Two-person custody. Never store alongside K-UPDATE-SIGN — the separation is the point.

keys.name: Secure Boot / PBL platform keys
keys.purpose: Signs PblApp.efi and the persist capsule; owns the db enrollment that makes firmware trust the platform.
keys.loss_impact: Firmware stops trusting the platform. Recovery is a manual enrolment visit per machine — the exact cost PBL exists to avoid.
keys.transfer_action: Transfers with the signing authority ruling (see `.devin/PENDING-RULING.md`, D-130). Losing it also invalidates the claim that fleet firmware trust is provisioned.

keys.name: Azure Artifact Signing account + certificate profile
keys.purpose: Signs the Windows agent/installer binaries so Windows trusts them without a SmartScreen reputation reset.
keys.loss_impact: Release pipeline cannot produce signed Windows artifacts; SmartScreen reputation restarts from zero for every distributed build.
keys.transfer_action: Identity validation is tied to a legal entity. Either the Azure account transfers inside that entity or the company re-validates and re-signs; either way hashes change.

keys.name: Apple Developer ID (p12 + app-specific password)
keys.purpose: Signs and notarizes the Electron desktop shell for macOS.
keys.loss_impact: macOS builds stop being notarized; Gatekeeper blocks them on the target machine.
keys.transfer_action: Enrollment belongs to a legal entity. Transfer the team or re-enroll under the company's Apple Developer Program.

keys.name: GitHub token for release downloads
keys.purpose: Lets the server download cross-platform agent binaries from GitHub Releases when the repo is private.
keys.loss_impact: Cross-platform installer generation fails with a 404 or a rate-limit; the fleet is unaffected.
keys.transfer_action: Issue a fresh fine-grained token scoped to the release repo. Never transfer a user PAT.

keys.name: Cloudflare Workers account + wrangler token
keys.purpose: Hosts the serverless transport/API surface when the product is deployed without a local server.
keys.loss_impact: The serverless deployment cannot be updated or rolled back; the running Worker keeps serving until the token is needed.
keys.transfer_action: Transfer the account (not the token) so billing and the Worker's own secrets move with it.

keys.name: PostgreSQL superuser/application password
keys.purpose: Database access for the API.
keys.loss_impact: Downtime for a password rotation; no permanent loss if rotated with `ALTER ROLE`.
keys.transfer_action: Rotate after transfer. The receiving team must own the database host, not just the credential.

keys.name: Google Geolocation API key
keys.purpose: WiFi triangulation (~20-50 m) instead of IP fallback (~10-50 km). Baked into generated agent installers.
keys.loss_impact: Tracking silently degrades to the IP fallback — accuracy drops by orders of magnitude and the dashboard still looks functional, which is the dangerous part.
keys.transfer_action: Billing is attached to the key's project. Transfer the GCP project or re-issue and re-generate installers for every device.

keys.name: Microsoft Graph (Intune) app registration
keys.purpose: Read-only device inventory import. The connector never issues lockdowns.
keys.loss_impact: Inventory import stops; nothing else degrades.
keys.transfer_action: Consent belongs to the receiving tenant — it must be granted by them, not transferred.

keys.name: MeshCentral login token/credentials
keys.purpose: Optional read-only inventory upstream. Off by default; 1.3.x has no REST API, so the connector cannot read inventory yet.
keys.loss_impact: An optional integration stops.
keys.transfer_action: Prefer revoking and issuing a new token on the receiving side.

keys.name: SMTP alert credentials
keys.purpose: Email alerts for stolen-device, lockdown-confirmed, stale-device, deadman and DB-degradation events.
keys.loss_impact: Alerting stops. The product still locks devices, but nobody is told — a silent failure in the one flow that matters most.
keys.transfer_action: The receiving company should send from its own domain (SPF/DKIM alignment), which means new credentials, not transferred ones.

keys.name: Slack / generic notification webhooks
keys.purpose: Alert delivery into the company's chat/SOC pipeline.
keys.loss_impact: Alerts are logged to console only.
keys.transfer_action: Always re-create in the receiving workspace; a transferred webhook URL is a live posting credential.

keys.name: Monitoring admin credentials
keys.purpose: Grafana admin login for the optional monitoring profile.
keys.loss_impact: Dashboards are read-only until reset. Note the shipped default is `admin/admin`.
keys.transfer_action: Reset on first login, which `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` already requires.

accounts.service: GitHub org + repo + Actions secrets + release artifacts
accounts.why: Source, CI, release binaries, and the update-download source the server calls.
accounts.transfer_action: Transfer repository ownership into the company org; re-create all 10 Actions secrets rather than exporting them.

accounts.why: Windows code signing identity + certificate profile.
accounts.transfer_action: Move the subscription or re-validate identity inside the company's tenant.

accounts.why: Developer ID signing + notarization for the Electron desktop shell.
accounts.transfer_action: Enrollment is per legal entity; re-enroll under the company.

accounts.why: Serverless transport deployment and its secrets.
accounts.transfer_action: Transfer account ownership; re-issue wrangler tokens.

accounts.why: The admin URL baked into installers, plus ACME/Caddy certificate issuance.
accounts.transfer_action: Transfer the registration and keep the DNS zone; ACME re-issues without cost.

accounts.why: WiFi triangulation key with billing attached.
accounts.transfer_action: Move the project or re-issue the key and regenerate every installer.

accounts.why: Alert delivery to the security team.
accounts.transfer_action: New account under the company's domain.

accounts.service: Microsoft Entra tenant + Graph app registration
accounts.why: Optional read-only Intune inventory import (consent is tenant-scoped).
accounts.transfer_action: Receiving tenant grants its own consent.

accounts.service: Linux host (Docker 24+ / compose v2, 2 GB RAM, 20 GB disk) or cloud equivalent
accounts.why: Runs the API, PostgreSQL and Caddy.
accounts.transfer_action: The company must own the host, the volume and the backup target — not just receive an image.

assets.what: FRANKENSTEIN — first production device (HP EliteBook, Win 11, service install)
assets.why: Carries the hardware verification evidence for 11 of 13 enforcement paths and is the reference service install.
assets.transfer_action: Re-image or hand over with documented BIOS state; the site licence/BIOS password must be recorded with it.

assets.why: Second hardware target covering the HP Sure Admin / UEFI path.
assets.transfer_action: Same as P-FRANKENSTEIN; record the Sure Admin credential location, never the value.

assets.what: A named sacrificial machine for E-BCD and E-HP-UEFI
assets.why: The two enforcement paths are NOT hardware-verified precisely because a failed run rewrites boot config or sets a firmware password needing a manual BIOS visit.
assets.transfer_action: Must be supplied by the receiving company, with a written recovery plan, or the two paths stay unit-test-only in writing.

obligations.obligation: Authority to issue a remote lockdown/recover command
obligations.evidence: audit ledger entry + dashboard actor id

obligations.obligation: Authority to sign and publish an agent update
Custody of the four critical key domains (pepper, field, location, backup) and the two trust roots (update-sign, recovery-escrow)
On-call response to a locked/stolen device event
Backup restore drill (encrypted backups, verify they decrypt)
obligations.evidence: restore transcript against a fresh DB

obligations.obligation: Hardware verification window on real devices
obligations.cadence: per release that touches an enforcement path

obligations.obligation: Green full-verify on a clean machine after any environment change
Employee-monitoring notice, lawful basis and works-council consultation (where applicable)
obligations.evidence: signed policy + DPIA in the company's name

obligations.obligation: Incident response plan and security contact

acceptances.item: Hippocratic Licence 2.1 usage restriction on react-leaflet / @react-leaflet/core (not OSI-approved, restricts use)
acceptances.note: Either replace the two dependencies or sign an explicit acceptance. Stated as an open product decision in LICENSE.

acceptances.item: E-BCD and E-HP-UEFI remain verified-in-unit-test only
acceptances.note: Accept in writing, or supply a sacrificial machine and recovery plan so they can be promoted to verified-on-hardware.

acceptances.item: No SSO/SAML/OIDC and no MFA on admin accounts at transfer
acceptances.note: Accept the gap with a dated remediation plan, or decline the transfer.

acceptances.item: Who is authorised to use covert tracking / lockdown against an individual, and under what policy
acceptances.note: The audit ledger and RBAC matrix are the technical answer; the company must adopt the policy answer.

acceptances.item: Whether the existing database transfers (keys K-AGENT-PEPPER, K-FIELD-ENC, K-LOCATION, K-BACKUP travel with it)
acceptances.note: A transfer of personal data is a controller change with its own notice obligations.

gaps.gap: No SSO/SAML/OIDC provider support; admins are local username/password.
gaps.remedy: Add an OIDC/SAML identity provider path behind the existing auth middleware.
TOTP enrolment on admin records + recovery codes.

gaps.gap: No licence/entitlement mechanism (no activation, seat count or expiry).
gaps.remedy: Decide the commercial model before building it; an offline activation file fits the on-prem shape.

gaps.gap: Single-tenant by construction; one company per deployment.
gaps.remedy: Not a small change: tenant scoping on every table plus a tenant-aware pool. On-prem avoids it entirely.

gaps.gap: No audit export (CSV/JSON) or DSAR tooling.
gaps.remedy: A read-only export route over the existing audit ledger.

gaps.gap: No SBOM generation in the release pipeline.
gaps.remedy: syft/cyclonedx at release time; both are free and offline-capable.

gaps.gap: No incident-response plan and no published vulnerability-disclosure policy.
gaps.remedy: Write both; `docs/SECURITY.md` is the raw material.

gaps.gap: AGENTS.md claims 37 OPEN PBL debt items; the ledger has 5 status markers OPEN.
gaps.blocks: Trust in the documentation set at transfer
gaps.remedy: Reconcile the count before handover, or the receiving team stops trusting the rest.
